title: SecOps-NG Codebase Disclosure Timeline Record (SKELETON)
description: Typed shape for one per-finding disclosure-timeline record emitted by the codebase vulnerability management workflow (F-WF-07). One record is produced per (sbom_content_hash, component, version, advisory_id) finding — one entry produced by the assess-disclosure / track-timeline states of playbook.codebase_vuln_management@v1 — and carries the advisory anchor, the affected component+version pinned against the operator's SBOM, the assessed severity tier, and the disclosure-window deadlines the operator's coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure (CVD) policy commits to. SKELETON in this card: the field inventory and patterns are pinned, but no compiler emission, no scanner-CLI invocation, and no per-target byte-parity golden ships — those land in the F-WF-07 CORE-FANOUT and EXTEND-tests-goldens siblings. Public-bar artifact: operator-side strings (owner labels, advisory references) MUST stay role-shaped or URN-shaped; individual personal names, credential-shaped strings, and raw SBOM payloads carrying personal data are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected at the schema boundary.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject records produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship.

id.description: Stable per-record identifier. Convention: SHA-256 hex digest of `<workflow_id>|<sbom_content_hash>|<component.purl>|<advisory_id>` (UTF-8, no separators around the pipes). Deterministic on those four inputs so a re-walk of the same SBOM against the same advisory re-derives the same id and dedup is trivial.

stream.description: Identifies which evidence stream produced the record. Constant on this schema.

workflow_id.description: Stable workflow identifier — the lower-snake-case workflow stable-id from `content/playbooks/<workflow>/`. Constant for this stream at `codebase_vuln_management`; carried explicitly so downstream rollups can join records across streams without re-deriving the source workflow.

sbom_content_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the SBOM artefact bytes the finding was derived from, pinned at ingest-sbom and carried through the workflow. Anchors the record to a specific SBOM revision so a re-build that changes a dependency version produces a new record set rather than mutating the existing one.

advisory_id.description: Canonical advisory identifier for the vulnerability. Accepts CVE (`CVE-YYYY-NNNN+`), GHSA (`GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`), or OSV (`OSV-YYYY-NNNN+`); operators MAY substitute a vendor advisory id when no canonical advisory has been assigned. The same advisory against two distinct components yields two distinct records.

component.description: The affected component+version pair as pinned against the SBOM. PURL-shaped so the record joins back into the SBOM artefact at sbom_content_hash without ambiguity.

purl.description: Package URL (PURL) for the affected component, mirror of the SBOM's per-component identifier. RFC-shaped, lowercase scheme + type, no embedded credentials.

version.description: Affected version as pinned against the SBOM. Carried as a string so non-semver ecosystems (debian epoch versions, maven qualifiers) round-trip unchanged.

severity.description: Assessed severity tier produced by assess-disclosure. Mirrors the four-band CVSS-derived vocabulary used elsewhere in the content model (kpi.vuln_disclosure_sla, kri.cvd_intake_aging). The operator-side regression-band table for severity-to-disclosure-window resolution lives with the CVD policy, not with this schema.

disclosure_window.description: Disclosure-window deadlines this finding has acquired under the operator's CVD policy. The `policy_ref` pins which CVD-policy revision the deadlines were computed against; `acknowledge_by` / `fix_by` / `disclose_by` are ISO-8601 UTC absolute timestamps so downstream metrics can compute on-time / breach without re-walking the policy.

policy_ref.description: Stable id of the CVD-policy revision the disclosure-window deadlines were computed against. Reuses the policy namespace (`policy.<slug>@v<semver>`) so reviewers can re-derive which policy text was in force.

acknowledge_by.description: Deadline by which the operator's CVD policy commits to acknowledging the finding internally and (where applicable) to an external reporter. ISO-8601 UTC, second precision.

fix_by.description: Deadline by which the operator's CVD policy commits to a remediation (security update, mitigating control, or formal accept-risk decision). ISO-8601 UTC, second precision.

disclose_by.description: Deadline by which the operator's CVD policy commits to coordinated public disclosure (advisory publication, security-update dissemination per CRA Annex I §2(7)). ISO-8601 UTC, second precision.

source_data.description: Source-data shape pointer for the finding. Mirror of the effectiveness-snapshot `measurement.source_shape` discipline (G-04 metric field shape). The underlying advisory payload is deliberately not embedded here — the source-shape pointer is the public-bar-safe surface, and any personal data in the raw payload is out of scope per AGENTS.md §3.

kind.description: Which source-shape vocabulary the pointer reads against.

ocsf_class_uid.description: OCSF event-class identifier. Optional, carried when `kind == ocsf`; absent otherwise. For codebase findings the reference class is OCSF Vulnerability Finding (class_uid 2002).

telemetry_ref.description: Long-form telemetry URN. Optional, carried when `kind == telemetry`; absent otherwise.

ref_viz.description: Visualisation pointer — opaque to this schema, consumed by the downstream dashboard / auditor-bundle surfaces to look up the canonical view of this record. Convention: `viz.<slug>@v<semver>`. The dashboards themselves are out of scope at this layer; the field is reserved here so the EXTEND-docs-cookbook sibling has a stable hook to point at.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the assess-disclosure step resolved the record. Format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` (no sub-second precision, no offset — UTC only). Pinned at emission so downstream on-time / breach computations against `disclosure_window` are reproducible.
